# lines.types: Plane

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> An infinite plane in Hesse normal form: the points p with Dot(Normal, p)
> equal to Distance. Distance is the signed distance from the world origin to
> the plane along Normal. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hesse\_normal\_form)

### Line 89

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/lines.types.plato, line 89](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/lines.types.plato#L89).

```plato

//==
// # Planes, half-spaces, and slabs
//
// The two-dimensional flat (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plane_(geometry)) and the
// regions it bounds: the half-plane and half-space on and behind a boundary flat,
// the slab between two parallel flats, and the record a plane-intersection query
// returns.

//==
// # Planes and half-spaces

// An infinite plane in Hesse normal form: the points p with Dot(Normal, p)
// equal to Distance. Distance is the signed distance from the world origin to
// the plane along Normal. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hesse_normal_form)
type Plane
    implements IGeometry3D, IConnected, IManifold, IOrientable, INearestPoint3D
{
    // The plane's UNIT normal (unit by Direction3D's own invariant); it points into
    // the plane's front / positive half-space.
    Normal: Direction3D;

    // The SIGNED distance from the WORLD ORIGIN to the plane, measured along Normal
    // (the Hesse form's d) -- NOT the distance from an arbitrary reference point,
    // and easy to misread as a generic offset. Because Normal is a unit vector this
    // is a true length in the coordinate frame's own units, and the signed distance
    // of any point p is SignedDistance(plane, p) = Dot(Normal, p) - Distance.
    Distance: Number;
}
```
